newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada governor says debt-GDP too high.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada governor says debt-GDP too high.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said on Wednesday Canada's current debt to gross domestic product ratio remains too high although it is difficult to say what the optimum ratio is.
Thiessen also told a Toronto Board of Trade meeting that the central bank does not favor negative real interest rates.

"If you look back in history, particularly in inflationary times, you can actually find times when that calculation left you with a negative real interest rate. Well, when I look back on those times, what I see are policy mistakes," Thiessen said.
The governor made the remarks in response to audience questions following his speech to a group of Toronto businessman.
The central banker applauded recent moves by goverments to lower the ratio of debt to GDP. He said the ratio will have to decline further before an optimum rate becomes appearant.

"What we do know is the current ratio is too high. We can see it when we get hit with negative shocks at of one kind or another. Investors get very nervous about holding debt in a country where the public debt-to-GDP ratio is over 100. So we know the current level is too high," said Thiessen.
The ratio of provincial and federal government debt to Canadian GDP was about 103 percent in 1995. Thiessen said the ratio should decline in coming years.
